statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-40612: in jq 1.8.1 and earlier, jv_contains, which backs contains() and inside(), recurses into nested arrays and objects with no depth limit, so a deeply nested value (built with reduce) exhausts the C stack and crashes jq (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/security/advisories/GHSA-r7m6-x9c7-h69j). Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/jqlang/jq/commit/d1a12569d91641135976a8536776a4a329c02cc2, 'Limit the containment check depth', which names this CVE and makes contains() fail with 'Containment check too deep' past depth 10000; it is first released in jq 1.8.2. Checked libjq.so.1.0.4 in the jq package (which /usr/bin/jq links) and libjq.a in jq-dev for every jq build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 1.8.1-r0, 1.8.1_git20260429-r1, 1.8.2_git20260622-r1 and 1.8.2_git20261021-r2, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. The two 1.8.1 builds lack the depth-limit code and both 1.8.2 builds carry it. The range ends at 1.8.2_git20260622-r1.

CVE-2026-40612: in jq 1.8.1 and earlier, jv_contains, which backs contains() and inside(), recurses into nested arrays and objects with no depth limit, so a deeply nested value (built with reduce) exhausts the C stack and crashes jq (https://github.com/jqlang/jq/security/advisories/GHSA-r7m6-x9c7-h69j). Debian fixed trixie in 1.7.1-6+deb13u3 (DSA-6416-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-40612); DHI has not published a rebuild of that update. Checked libjq.so.1.0.4 in libjq1 for every jq build published in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64: the rebuilds of Debian 1.7.1-6+deb13u2 and an arm64-only build versioned 1.8.1-5 lack the depth-limit code, and the DHI build of jq 1.8.2-1 (amd64 and arm64) carries it. The range ends at that 1.8.2-1 build, the first published build with the fix.
